name: Male fertility
about: The XY reproductive system: desire, the hypothalamus–pituitary signals, the testes and the testosterone and sperm they make, sperm maturation and transport, the prostate and seminal vesicles, and erection. Built from Open Targets disease genetics and Gene Ontology, not from the library.
rule: Gene Ontology mechanism genes, plus Open Targets genes scoring ≥ 0.5 (≥ 0.8 genetic for level and timing traits)

mechanisms.name: Desire and sexual behaviour
mechanisms.about: Male mating behaviour and other reproductive behaviour.
mechanisms.explain: Desire runs on testosterone acting in the brain, dopamine reward signalling and oxytocin. GO's male mating behaviour genes come mostly from mouse studies. Variants here shift intensity, not whether drive is there.

mechanisms.name: Hypothalamus–pituitary signals
mechanisms.about: GnRH, LH and FSH release and response, and steroid hormone receptor signalling.
mechanisms.explain: GnRH pulses from the hypothalamus release LH and FSH. LH makes Leydig cells produce testosterone; FSH, together with testosterone, drives Sertoli cells to support sperm production. Testosterone and inhibin feed back. Changes here link to hypogonadism and lower sperm counts; the FSHB −211 variant lowers FSH, for example.

mechanisms.name: Testosterone production
mechanisms.about: Making testosterone, DHT and their precursors.
mechanisms.explain: Leydig cells turn cholesterol into testosterone (StAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, HSD17B3). SRD5A2 converts some into the stronger DHT, and aromatase turns some into estradiol. SHBG in the blood decides how much is free. Variants here move testosterone levels.

mechanisms.name: Testis development
mechanisms.about: Building the testis, male sex determination, and Leydig and Sertoli cells.
mechanisms.explain: Genes that make the testis and keep it male (SRY, SOX9, NR5A1), and that build the Leydig and Sertoli cells. Strong defects cause differences of sex development and undescended testes.

mechanisms.name: Sperm production
mechanisms.about: Spermatogenesis: from stem cell through meiosis to a finished sperm.
mechanisms.explain: Making a sperm takes about 74 days: stem cells divide, go through meiosis and remodel into sperm, nursed by Sertoli cells. Hundreds of genes take part, so most male-infertility genes sit here; variants link to low or absent sperm counts.

mechanisms.name: Sperm maturation and motility
mechanisms.about: The epididymis, and the tail and energy that let sperm swim.
mechanisms.explain: Sperm swim with a tail (flagellum) powered by mitochondria, and gain that ability while they mature in the epididymis. Genes here cover the tail, its energy supply and maturation; defects cause poor motility.

mechanisms.name: Capacitation and fertilization
mechanisms.about: Capacitation, the acrosome reaction, and binding the egg.
mechanisms.explain: In the female tract sperm capacitate, then the acrosome reaction releases enzymes that cut through the egg's coat before the sperm binds and fuses. Genes here cover those steps.

mechanisms.name: Prostate and seminal vesicles
mechanisms.about: Building the glands that make seminal fluid.
mechanisms.explain: The prostate and seminal vesicles make most of the seminal fluid and its enzymes, which protect sperm and liquefy the ejaculate. Genes here cover the glands' development.

mechanisms.name: Erection
mechanisms.about: Nitric oxide and smooth-muscle signalling for erection.
mechanisms.explain: Erection needs nitric oxide from nerves and the vessel lining (NOS3), cGMP signalling in the smooth muscle (broken down by PDE5), and good blood flow. Genes here link to erectile dysfunction, which shares risk with blood vessel health.

disease_explain: Open Targets ties these genes to one of the theme's conditions, mostly through GWAS, but Gene Ontology has no reproductive mechanism for them yet. Treat them as signals to follow up rather than explained pathways.

organs.name: Hypothalamus and pituitary
organs.about: GnRH from the hypothalamus releases LH and FSH from the pituitary, which run the testes.

organs.name: Testes
organs.about: Leydig cells make testosterone; Sertoli cells nurse sperm through about 74 days of production.

organs.name: Epididymis and vas deferens
organs.about: Sperm mature and learn to swim in the epididymis, then travel up the vas deferens.

organs.name: Prostate and seminal vesicles
organs.about: Make most of the seminal fluid that carries and protects sperm.
